source.analysis_subject: bench: close Gate decoder and GDN state layouts
source.scan_method: Read each selected safetensors payload directly by header data_offsets; count all 256 raw FP8 codes; choose the 127 most frequent codes independently per tensor with raw-code ascending tie break; compute exact component lengths and 256-byte final tensor alignment. No GPU kernel, persistent sidecar, source edit, or test edit was used.
source.qkv_z_tensor_selector: 48 linear-attention layers times in_proj_qkv.weight and in_proj_z.weight

format.semantics: lossless raw FP8-byte reconstruction before the existing decoded-value lookup; no quantization, approximation, pruning, MTP, or arithmetic-order change

palette.selection: descending raw-byte frequency, then ascending raw byte for deterministic ties
palette.codes: seven-bit indices 0..126 select common raw FP8 bytes; index 127 is the escape sentinel

format.row_contract: each source row is divisible into 128-value tiles; QKV/Z K=5120 gives 40 tiles per row
format.code_stream: seven bits per source value, packed without padding in logical row order; 112 bytes per 128-value tile

escape_directory.row_escape_base: one u32 byte offset per source row into the tensor raw-escape pool
escape_directory.tile_prefix: one u16 count of prior escapes within the row per 128-value tile
escape_directory.u16_safety: a row contains only 5120 source values, so its escape count is at most 5120
escape_directory.raw_escape_pool: one original FP8 byte for each sentinel, stored in logical source order

component_formula_per_tensor.encoded_bytes: sum of components rounded up once to 256 bytes

format.direct_decode_mapping: For each existing warp-owned 128-value row tile, 28 lanes cooperatively load the 112-byte code stream; warp shuffles reconstruct four seven-bit indices per consuming lane. Ballot/prefix rank addresses the rare raw escape. Common codes may use a 127-entry decoded shared palette; escaped raw bytes take the exact existing FP8 decode path.
format.production_topology_boundary: retain QKV1536/Z768 logical grid behavior, 256 threads, the two-phase reduction-scratch ping-pong order, the BF16 A/B tail, one kernel node, all BF16-RNE boundaries, and all output addresses
format.sector_note: code tiles are contiguous within each row. Adjacent warps consume adjacent 112-byte spans, so the shared boundary sector can remain an L1 hit; do not pad every tile to 128 bytes because that would erase the main-stream byte reduction.

decision.reason: All 96 QKV/Z tensors pass the frozen <=92-percent per-tensor capacity gate. The exact all-layer representation removes 385,034,240 bytes/token and has a 2.197907-ms payload-only ceiling, while only 0.30 ms or 1.01307x stage speedup is required. Its approximately 39.54-us/layer decoder-overhead budget is materially wider than O projection and it avoids every already rejected no-byte layout, cache, staging, grid, fusion, buffering, and lookahead mechanism.
decision.o_projection: retain as rank-2 backup because its exact scan passes but its decoder-overhead budget is only about 12.46 us/layer

claim_limits: This is a zero-code payload-capacity admission, not a GPU performance result or production promotion.
The encoded byte counts include the exact defined code stream, tile prefixes, row bases, palette, raw escapes, and final 256-byte tensor alignment, but no sidecar was materialized or retained.
The ideal millisecond savings linearly divide removed bytes by the current measured stage payload bandwidth and assume zero decode overhead. They are screening ceilings, not achieved latency.
Tensor entropy and frequency results are specific to the hash-pinned model revision.
MTP, generic fusion, system buffering, and closed cache/layout candidates are excluded from this path.
